look_here_first: Locate several stem nodes: leaves alternate, typically narrow and softly hairy on upright branched shoreline shoots. At flowering, see a showy four-petaled yellow corolla and the conspicuously long inferior ovary BELOW the sepals; usually eight stamens. Compare L. repens opposite nodes and tiny four-stamen flowers.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: alternate narrow leaves up upright branched stem

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: large four-petaled yellow flower with eight stamens

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: long inferior ovary / elongated seed capsule

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: local stems usually five-ridged; confirm rather than assume

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Local Williamson County specimens have strongly five-ridged, usually hairy stems; Flora of North America allows terete or ridged stems across the species.

key_traits.label: Flower
key_traits.text: Usually four broad showy yellow petals; locally around 23–39 mm across and commonly eight stamens in two sets (rarely five sepals/petals and ten stamens).

key_traits.label: Ovary
key_traits.text: Inferior, distinctly elongated and often low eight-ribbed on four-sided base; distinguish from Ludwigia repens very short four-angled inferior ovary.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Long narrow cylindrical to club-shaped many-seeded capsule, 38–45 mm in Williamson specimens; local plants typically show 8 valve splits, but FNA describes 4–8 valves across broader species.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey explicitly uses this plant to teach an inferior ovary, showing the ovary below the visible flower parts at close range.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Erect, much-branched, often taprooted wetland herb/subshrub, usually growing on moist shorelines; forms can vary.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Alternate helically, one leaf per successive node; contrast the opposite pairs of Ludwigia repens.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Usually narrow oblanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, mostly entire, with very short petioles; often short hairy and not glossy.
